entries.title: Nonnegative grand-canonical DLR specification
entries.statement: For a locally finite exterior eta, finite z>0 and beta>0, and nonnegative pair potential v, the conditional law in bounded B assigns the n-particle sector unnormalized density z^n/n! times exp(-beta H_B), where H_B is the sum of internal pair interactions and interactions with eta. The empty configuration has weight one. There is no neutralizing background or fixed particle-count constraint; the partition sum includes n=0.
assumptions: Ordinary grand-canonical DLR law on locally finite configurations
Nonnegative pair interaction, zero empty energy
No neutralizing background, negative external energy, or fixed local count

entries.title: Draft: uniform DLR void bound and arbitrarily large holes
entries.statement: DRAFT campaign derivation, awaiting independent reviewer w536. For an ordinary grand-canonical DLR law with finite z>0, finite beta>0, nonnegative pair interaction, zero empty energy, no background and no fixed local count, 1<=Xi_B<=exp(z|B|), so the conditional void probability is at least exp(-z|B|). For m disjoint equal-volume regions of volume V, the probability all are occupied is at most (1-exp(-zV))^m, by exterior conditioning and induction, without independence. Countably many tails and integer radii imply arbitrarily large empty balls almost surely. Such a configuration cannot be a uniformly bounded displacement of any full-rank lattice, even a configuration-dependent lattice. This covers ordinary three-dimensional Riesz DLR laws with s>3; it does not rule out lattice-periodic probability laws or address renormalized s<=3 specifications. Equality of the universal finite bound holds for the zero-potential Poisson specification.
assumptions: Ordinary grand-canonical DLR law on locally finite configurations
Nonnegative pair interaction, zero empty energy
No neutralizing background, negative external energy, or fixed local count

entries.title: Auxiliary global-displacement bridge under audit
entries.statement: Auxiliary bridge to audit, not a statement of P0309: an ordinary finite-temperature, finite-activity grand-canonical Gibbs law with nonnegative pair interaction is supported on configurations admitting a bijection from some full-rank lattice whose displacement is bounded everywhere. This requirement is stronger than invariance of a probability law under lattice translations. The companion DRAFT void result proposes a refutation under the explicit ordinary-DLR assumptions; independent review is pending. No implication is asserted for a fixed-count or renormalized long-range specification.
assumptions: Ordinary grand-canonical DLR law on locally finite configurations
Nonnegative pair interaction, zero empty energy
No neutralizing background, negative external energy, or fixed local count

relations.rationale: The conditional void estimate uses the n=0 weight and nonnegative interaction of this exact specification.
The auxiliary bridge is explicitly restricted to the same ordinary grand-canonical specification.
Draft refutation pending independent review: arbitrarily large holes contradict the finite covering radius plus globally bounded displacement; the original P0309 target is not refuted.
Both address a limitation of using local harmonic localization to conclude a full Gibbs crystal: the prior card explicitly leaves defect and competing-configuration control open.
P0309 seeks low-positive-temperature Riesz crystalline Gibbs phases; this draft constrains one stronger configuration-support criterion in its ordinary s>3 regime.
